span.p:
eviction is a bet on correctness,
not on latency - it is irreversible

dropping reweights the survivors -
the softmax denominator shrinks

span.p:
attention sinks stay pinned -
load-bearing, not hot

span.p:
every policy stays bypassable -
the full-cache oracle is the instrument

display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
WRITE-TIME ADMISSION
sees k_i, v_i only. O(d), no attention matrix
hosts L2-norm, KeyDiff, EpiKV

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
staging buffer - hold k steps, then flush
k steps of extra residency buys k steps of context

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
DEFERRED EVICTION
sees prompt-side or k-step-lagged attention
hosts H2O, SnapKV, PyramidKV, ChunkKV, KVpop

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
resident set - budget B, per layer and per head
12 global layers grow with context, 36 stay at 512
budget against the 62 GiB-or-more fast tier at ~200 GB/s [M];
keep any single tensor under 32 GiB [M]

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
READ-TIME SELECTION
sees the actual q_t
hosts Quest, SparQ, RocketKV stage 2

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
TELEMETRY, mandatory - two scalars per step, per layer, per head.
Error is at most (1 - A) x max distance from a dropped v_i to the retained output.

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
PROTEUS produces k_i, v_i
8 KV heads x head_dim 128 x 2 B = 192 KiB per token, exact
48 layers: 12 full_attention, 36 sliding_attention at window 512

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: PROTEUS emits q_t - one query per decode step

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
PROTEUS computes o_t = sum of a_i v_i
over whatever Mnemosyne returned

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The hook that does NOT work:
score(keys, values, attention) -> subset

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
dropped - no backing store, no miss path, no hit-rate metric.
The only refetch is re-prefilling the whole prefix.

div.style: color: rgb(17, 17, 17) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
OUT OF CONTRACT - FastKV / Token-Selective Propagation.
A token not propagated past layer L never has KV computed for L+1..48:
not evicted, never produced. It edits Proteus's forward pass.

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A - retained attention mass
every score-based policy optimises this

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
dropped-value distance
no published policy reports this one

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
compression is TWO numbers, always -
bytes held vs bytes read per step
RocketKV: 400x against 32.6%
